title: gpu-oom-debug-notes-julia-hart
body:
Context:
- Repro on dedicated pool (p3dn-equivalent) when running long-context chat generation with model xlm-13b-quant. Happens intermittently after ~1500 tokens per session.
- Seen on both local dev and dedicated infra; more frequent on instances with mixed driver versions.

Hypothesis / quick notes:
- Likely a combination of insufficient GPU memory + unexpected allocation pattern (KV cache growth + batching).
- Also observed cuda/driver mismatch warnings in dmesg on one host (nvidia driver 515 vs CUDA 11.8 artifacts from container). Might cause fallback allocations or fragmentation.
- Quantized kernels may allocate pinned host memory for workspace; if driver older, behavior can be unstable.

Commands tried / logs:
1) Repro command (internal run script):
   ./run_inference.sh --model xlm-13b-quant --context 8192 --batch 1 --streaming

2) docker inspect + container env:
   docker exec -it <cid> bash -c "nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,memory.total,memory.used --format=csv"
   Output example: "Tesla V100, 515.76, 32768 MiB, 1024 MiB"

3) dmesg snippet (on host after crash):
   [ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU at 0000:00:1e.0: RmInitAdapter failed! (0x01:0x54:123)
   [ 1234.567892] NVRM: The NVIDIA probe routine failed for 1 device(s).

4) Container stderr when OOM triggered:
   RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.34 GiB (GPU 0; 31.75 GiB total capacity; 29.80 GiB already allocated; 256.00 MiB free)
   During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
   RuntimeError: CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version

5) torch.cuda.memory_summary() (trimmed):
   | .Allocated: 29.80 GiB
   | .Cached: 0.65 GiB
   | .Active: 30.45 GiB
   Peak: 30.61 GiB
   Allocations: many small tensors during kv cache extension -> fragmentation suspected.

6) nvprof / nvidia-smi during run (non-repro run):
   - occasional spikes to 99% memory usage, but host shows fragmentation after GC.

Actions tried so far (and results):
- Reduced batch size to 1 -> OOM still occurs at long contexts (delays but doesn't eliminate).
- Force torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = False / deterministic -> no change.
- Tried CLI flag --max-new-tokens 1024 -> reduces frequency but still hits for sessions with long rollouts.
- Upgraded container CUDA toolkit from 11.6 to 11.8 (image rebuilt) -> consistent runtime warning: "CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version" on host with 515 driver.
- On a host with driver 525.105, container runs longer before OOM.
- Tried setting TORCH_USE_CUDA_DSA=1 (debug) -> caused different failure path, not helpful.
- Experimented with prefix caching off (disable kv cache) -> no OOM, confirms kv cache heavily contributes.

Root-cause candidates:
- Driver mismatch: container expects newer CUDA runtime than installed driver on some hosts -> leads to degraded behavior and possibly allocation failures.
- True memory exhaustion because quantized model uses more ephemeral workspace memory than expected for certain kernels.
- Fragmentation due to many small allocations during kv-cache growth + frequent allocations from batching.

Immediate mitigation suggestions:
- Ensure host drivers are >= runtime requirement (bump to 525+ where we saw improvement). Rolling kernel/driver upgrade for dedicated fleet.
- Add guard rails in serving runtime: pre-check available memory vs estimated peak for given context length + model quantization profile. Reject / degrade requests with explicit 413 or fallback to smaller-model variant.
- Enable early KV checkpointing: stream out older KV segments to host pinned memory (if possible) or spill to CPU memory with async transfers.
- Implement more aggressive pooling to reduce small ephemeral allocations (reuse buffers, reserve workspace at model load).
- Improve logging: capture torch.cuda.memory_snapshot() and driver/runtime mismatch warnings and surface in trace for each failed request.

Longer-term work / experiments to run:
- Reproduce in controlled environment: create matrix of driver versions (515, 520, 525), CUDA runtimes (11.6, 11.8, 12.x), and record failure modes.
- Run synthetic allocation stress test that mimics kv-cache growth to confirm fragmentation hypothesis.
- Try different quantization kernels (if available) that use smaller workspace.
- Investigate cudaMallocAsync (requires newer driver) to reduce fragmentation and reduce GC stalls.

Notes / breadcrumbs:
- Related tickets: JIRA-INF-4123 (OOM incidents), JIRA-INF-4180 (driver upgrade plan).
- Linked PR where we attempted pre-reserve buffer: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/987 (rolled back after crash on 515 hosts).
- Slack thread: #infra-gpu (see pinned message from 2026-01-12).

Immediate TODOs:
- [ ] Coordinate minimal driver upgrade schedule with infra (target 525.85+)
- [ ] Add memory headroom estimation to per-request admission logic (short-term feature)
- [ ] Add structured logs for driver/runtime mismatch and capture nvidia-smi + dmesg when a failure is detected
- [ ] Run repro matrix and attach results to JIRA-INF-4123

Quick reference commands for infra team:
- Check driver vs runtime:
  nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv && docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:11.8.0-base nvidia-smi
- Dump kernel modules / dmesg filter:
  dmesg | egrep -i "nvrm|nvidia|cuda" | tail -n 200
- Capture memory snapshot from pytorch inside container (on failure):
  python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.memory_summary())"

Notes to self: capture one full crash trace with container id and host dmesg + nvidia-smi in single artifacts bundle. That made root cause triage easier last time.

---
Versions observed when last repro'd:
- Model: xlm-13b-quant (custom quant profile v2)
- Container CUDA: 11.8
- Host driver: 515.76 (bad), 525.85 (better)
- PyTorch: 2.1.0+cu118
- NCCL: 2.14
- Kernel: Ubuntu 20.04 LTS (5.15.x)

End of notes.
